operations.summary: Updates legacy_name for one profile; new release reads display_name so this write is invisible unless backfilled or dual-written.
Updates display_name for one profile; old release never maintains this column.
SELECTs batch with display_name IS NULL then copies legacy_name to display_name with guarded UPDATE per row.

conflicts.risk_explanation: Backfill SELECTs rows with display_name IS NULL then UPDATEs display_name from stale legacy_name while v2 concurrently writes a user-supplied display_name to the same id. Without the AND display_name IS NULL guard the backfill would clobber the user value; test 1 forces this race with distinct values.

Backfill reads legacy_name to populate display_name while v1 concurrently changes legacy_name on the same row. SELECT-then-UPDATE in separate transactions is non-atomic so backfill can copy a stale legacy value leaving display_name permanently stale because later backfills skip NOT NULL rows.

Old release updates legacy_name, new release updates display_name, and backfill updates display_name on the same id. Concurrent UPDATEs to the same row contend on the row lock; a read-modify-write implementation would lose the different-column update.

tests.name: backfill_must_not_overwrite_concurrent_display_name
tests.rationale: Same NULL row is selected by backfill and concurrently set by v2 to a distinct custom value. Correct guarded backfill ends with custom in all serial orders (backfill-then-v2 overwrites to custom, v2-then-backfill skips). An unguarded backfill interleaved as SELECT NULL, v2 commit, UPDATE would clobber custom with alice_legacy.

invariants.description: user display_name must survive; backfill must not overwrite it with stale legacy value
legacy_name untouched by either actor except backfill read

tests.name: concurrent_legacy_and_display_updates_both_persist
tests.rationale: Old and new releases update different columns of the same row concurrently. Correct Postgres row UPDATEs preserve both columns in every order. A read-modify-write or full-row overwrite would lose one column.

tests.name: backfill_skips_set_row_and_fills_null_row
tests.rationale: Row 1 already has display_name, row 2 is NULL. Backfill with large limit must only fill row 2 while v1 updates row 1 legacy concurrently on a different id. Checks WHERE display_name IS NULL filtering and no cross-row corruption.

invariants.description: concurrent legacy update on already-backfilled row must persist
backfill must not touch already-set display_name
NULL row must be backfilled from its legacy_name
